$comment: SIBLING REGISTRY — files and templates that must move together.
WHY THIS EXISTS — 2026-09-15. Of 173 behaviour commits in 60 hours, 27 were
PARTIAL and every one had the same shape: a fix landed on one code or prompt
path and not its sibling. The `fixing-sibling-paths` skill already described
the failure class in prose and did not prevent a single one of the 27 — prose
is advisory, and an agent that does not invoke the skill never reads it. This
file makes the sibling relationship DATA, so two mechanical consumers can use
it: scripts/admin/check-sibling-paths.js (pre-push gate) and
tests/unit/sibling-parity.test.ts (structural parity, runs in the normal suite).
ADDING A SET is one entry. Keep `reason` to one line and name the axis — the
gate prints both, so the person it blocks learns what to look at.
FIELDS
id        stable slug, used in the gate output
axis      the recurring split this set belongs to
reason    one line: why these move together
members   repo-relative paths; ALL must change together (see severity)
severity  'block' — the only accepted value. A 'warn' tier existed for one
day; the owner retired it on 2026-09-15: EVERY set blocks, and the
Siblings-Checked marker (same-commit or vouching) is the one escape.
The gate rejects any other value rather than reading it as block.
generators / critics
A set may declare these INSTEAD of `members` (axis
generator-vs-critic). The rule is different and looser on purpose:
a commit touching the set must touch at least ONE generator AND at
least ONE critic, not every member. Three judges of one generator
are not siblings of each other; each is a sibling of the generator.
The disease this treats: a rule is added to a judge and the
generator is never told, so the page is penalised for something it
was never asked to do.
parity    optional structural assertions for tests/unit/sibling-parity.test.ts:
metadataKeys: true  -> the ---METADATA--- JSON example in every
member declares the same top-level keys
anchors: ["..."]     -> every member contains each literal string
ruleAnchors: [{critic, generator, note}] -> for a generator-vs-critic
set, a rule named on the critic side must have
its counterpart instruction on the generator side
ESCAPE HATCH — put `Siblings-Checked: <reason>` in the commit message when the
siblings genuinely need no change. It is a statement, not a silencer: write why.
A push whose FULL range covers every member passes without a marker, so a fix
split across two commits in one push is fine.

sets.axis: per-page vs all-pages Art Director
sets.reason: scene-expansion.txt is the per-page gap-fill/fallback template for the same Art Director contract scene-briefs-all.txt drives on the live beats path; a rule or metadata field on one and not the other silently reads as absent on whichever path runs.

sets.axis: beats text writer vs trial writer
sets.reason: story-text-from-beats.txt (the live beats path, every full story) and story-trial.txt (the live /try funnel writer) both write page prose under the same shared rules; a prose rule that becomes a promptBuilders constant reaches a path only through the placeholder that path declares, so a new one is declared at both sites or it silently reads as absent there. This set now also carries the retired trial-vs-full-writer axis: the trial path has repeatedly lagged the full path by weeks. story-unified.txt / story-unified-imagefirst.txt were members until 2026-09-15, when both were deleted as unreachable (docs/decisions.md).

parity.anchorsNote: only {PAGE_OPENING_VARIETY} is genuinely declared by both live prose writers. {RISK_FRAMING} and {AD_COMPOSITION} were anchors of the deleted unified-writer sets and are NOT declared by story-text-from-beats.txt — the beats chain carries risk framing inside {TELLING_RULES} on the arc prompts and composition on the Art Director. Asserting them here would assert a parity into existence that does not hold.

sets.axis: arc-informed audit vs blind audit
sets.reason: story-text-audit.txt (arc-informed) and story-text-audit-blind.txt (the blind reader) feed ONE parser and ONE merge (parseFaultLines / mergeAuditFindings, textRefine.js), and that merge dedupes on the CATEGORY TAG: same page + same category + different auditor is folded into one finding. So the FAULT-line output contract and the category vocabulary are shared state — a category name that gains a meaning on one side and not the other either folds two distinct faults into one or splits one fault into two. The question SETS are deliberately different, which is what the Siblings-Checked marker is for; the contract they share is not. STYLE is the one category that does NOT fold on the tag (2026-09-26, sameFault): a STYLE finding is one quoted sentence, and textRefine's $0 one-sentence-paragraph counter files STYLE lines too (source style-counter), so two STYLE findings are one fault only when they quote the same sentence.

sets.axis: lector prompt vs diff-pass prompt
sets.reason: story-text-proofread.txt (the lector) and story-text-diff.txt (the grammar check after the repair) are the two language passes over the finished text: a rule about what counts as a language fault, or what a correction may change, belongs on both. Since 2026-09-23 they no longer share an output contract - the grammar check edits numbered sentences (parseDiffEdits / applyDiffEdits) and cannot write a sentence neither version had; the lector keeps quoted spans (parseLectorFindings / applyLectorFindings).

sets.axis: quality-eval inventory vs unified inventory
sets.reason: image-evaluation.txt and image-inventory-unified.txt both describe the per-figure inventory the blind judge (image-prompt-compliance.txt) consumes; a schema change on one makes the two inventories incomparable.

sets.axis: Art Director VB authoring vs writer VB authoring
sets.reason: the Visual Bible is authored at two LIVE sites — the all-pages Art Director on the beats path (every full story) and the trial writer — and a rule about what a VB entry must state has to exist at both. The two pre-beats unified writers were members until 2026-09-15, when they were deleted as unreachable (docs/decisions.md).

parity.anchorsNote: the VB entry keys both live authoring sites genuinely declare today. `"size"` was anchored until 2026-09-15 and was dropped when the free-text size field was replaced by the `scaleClass` enum as the single source of scale truth; story-trial.txt still declares a PER-PAGE `size` on its scene-hint objects, which is a different field with a different consumer and is deliberately not anchored here. `"states"` is anchored since 2026-09-15 — owner ruling, every bible-authoring site declares it. `"vantages"` stays deliberately NOT anchored: it is absent from visual-bible.txt, which is a real divergence, not a parity target to assert into existence.

sets.axis: production repair vs user regeneration vs entity char-fix
sets.reason: repairPipeline.js, routes/regeneration.js and entityConsistency.js each invoke character repair by their own assembly; a guard or gate added to one leaves the other two entry points unguarded.

sets.axis: cover path vs page path cast assembly
sets.reason: coverComposite.js and compositeCastBuilder.js both resolve a hint-string name to a character and both hand-roll parts of it; a resolver or costume-key fix on one leaves the other resolving by raw name.

sets.axis: trial idea route vs its Test Lab mirror
sets.reason: the /try idea route (server/routes/trial.js) and the Lab's idea stage (server/lib/testlab.js, marked `route mirror:`) hand-assemble the SAME character line, category context and landmark text; a copy kept by hand at both is how the raw storyTheme ID shipped into every life-skill prompt as "the child plays at being a farm" (2026-09-15). Shared text belongs in one constant both require.

sets.axis: wizard idea route vs trial idea route
sets.reason: both idea routes name real places in their prompt from the town list the story will read, picked by Jev's LB1 ranking when a prepare call made it ready and in today's order otherwise (jevSelection.pickIdeaLandmarks, docs/decisions.md 2026-09-27 "Jev selection built"); each route has its own prepare endpoint the client fires when the story kind is picked (StoryWizard.tsx / TrialWizard.tsx). The trial route resolved a DIFFERENT list (getIndexedLandmarks(loc, 3) — the municipality rung) until 2026-09-27 and named places its story never had: a change to how one route picks, resolves or prepares its places belongs on the other.

sets.axis: regular avatar trait write vs trial trait write
sets.reason: a photo's apparentAge reaches character.physical at two sites: the regular avatar paths (routes/avatars.js, clampApparentAge on the consensus traits) and the trial (trialAge.js applyTrialPhotoTraits / reclampTrialApparentAge, used by every trial.js writer). extractCharacterVisualProfile trusts apparentAge over the declared age because that clamp bounds it; the trial copied it unclamped from e894b0fe6 until 2026-09-26, and prod trial job_1790282439176_ppgelxibt drew a declared 5-year-old as a middle-aged man.

sets.axis: Test Lab stage vs production call site
sets.reason: testlab.js re-implements the call that evalPipeline.js makes in production; when they drift the Lab measures something production never runs (version pinning, cast lists, model ids).

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: image-generation.txt is the only instruction the illustrator receives; image-evaluation.txt, image-semantic.txt and image-prompt-compliance.txt are the three judges that score the result. A rule added to a judge and not to the generator penalises a page for something it was never asked to do.

ruleAnchors.note: D-24 is CATASTROPHIC/CRITICAL for a mark painted on a figure, and the template forbade lettering only. The generator half is one exported constant (NO_CHARACTER_MARKING_RULE, promptBuilders.js) filled into this placeholder; that it reaches the BUILT prompt is pinned in tests/unit/generator-critic-rule-reach.test.ts, because a placeholder nobody fills is stripped silently.
D-16b is MAJOR when a hand holds something the scene never named while a named object is absent. The generator half is HANDS_HOLD_ONLY_NAMED_RULE, same mechanism and same reach test.

D-34 is MAJOR when a creature is drawn far from the size its page gave it (half or less, twice or more). The generator half is the creature's line in the REQUIRED OBJECTS block, built by promptBuilders.elementPageScaleNote (band phrase + a yardstick against the people in frame, from the one table visualBible.SCALE_ADULT_HEIGHT_FRACTION); the judge reads the SAME sentence through its ELEMENT SIZES input (buildElementSizesBlock), and every repaint through buildElementSizeClauseForRepair. One builder, three readers; pinned in tests/unit/creature-size-{page,eval,repair}.test.ts and element-page-scale.test.ts.
D-21 measures an object listed in ELEMENT SIZES against the size given there. The generator half is that object's REQUIRED OBJECTS line, the same elementPageScaleNote sentence.
D-31 measures a vehicle listed in ELEMENT SIZES against the size given there. The generator half is that vehicle's REQUIRED OBJECTS line, the same elementPageScaleNote sentence.

D-05e is MAJOR/MINOR when a garment's front features are drawn on a figure seen from behind (or the reverse). The generator half is the WORN ITEMS line in the character reference list (wornItems.buildWornStateLines): for a wearer the brief draws from behind it carries the tag `seen from the back` and the garment's authored `back` look, never its front description. The judges read the same tag on that character's CLOTHING CONTRACT line (evalPipeline.buildEvalClothingContract). Both sides decide facing with wornItems.faceAwayNames -> storyAvatars.resolveCellPose. Pinned in tests/unit/worn-item-facing.test.ts.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: The brief checks (sceneBriefCheck.js, and briefChecks.js, which adds the scene review's rules the owner kept as code checks on 2026-09-28: negation_named, element_uncited, character_fields, cast_not_in_plan, required_text_undeclared, clothing_incomplete) critique the briefs scene-briefs-all.txt authors and send them back in the one re-ask; a check the critic applies that the Art Director was never given produces a finding no rewrite can satisfy. The scene review (scene-review.txt) was this set's critic until it was deleted on 2026-09-28.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: A group of more than three characters is staged at one depth in a wider shot, or seen from behind as it moves away, and never lined up facing the viewer (owner, 2026-09-27; docs/decisions.md). The rule is authored by both Art Director templates (rule 4) and both iterate templates, and judged by the brief check (scene-review.txt check 6d [group_staging] until the review was deleted on 2026-09-28); the four templates read ONE constant, shotVocabulary.GROUP_STAGING_RULE, through {GROUP_STAGING}. The brief check sceneBriefCheck.checkGroupStaging measures the same rule from structured fields (GROUP_WIDER_SHOTS, `perspective`, `looksAt`) and sends group_shot_too_close / group_facing_viewer to the one brief re-ask. tests/unit/group-staging.test.ts pins that the constant reaches every built prompt. The planner (story-beats.txt) read it too while it picked the shot; since 2026-09-27 (later the same day) code writes every shot and holds the group rule in the Jev shot assignment (jevDecisions.assign, GROUP_WIDER_SHOTS), so the planner is no longer a generator of this rule.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: story-text-proofread.txt and story-text-audit.txt judge prose written under story-text-from-beats.txt (the live writer on every full story) and story-trial.txt (the /try funnel); a style or structure rule the auditor enforces must be a rule the writer was given, or every story is corrected after the fact instead of written right. story-text-audit-blind.txt joined 2026-09-23: it reads the same writer text and faults CONTRADICTION and ENDING, which the writer is told (prompt audit 05). The generator was story-unified.txt until 2026-09-15, when that template was deleted as unreachable — it had not been the live prose writer since the beats pipeline shipped.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: text-refine.txt is the ONE stage that rewrites shipped page prose, and it rewrites it from the findings story-text-audit.txt / story-text-audit-blind.txt / story-text-proofread.txt produce. Until 2026-09-21 it had no criteria of its own: it sliced them out of outline-analysis-imagefirst.txt, a checklist written for the outline reviewer, so it was told to read blocks it is never sent and to answer in a shape it cannot return (A7). Its criteria now live in its own template, which removes the accidental coupling and creates a real drift risk in its place: a prose rule a text auditor deducts for must be a rule the rewriter was given, or the audit reports a fault the only stage that could fix it has never heard of. book-audit.txt joined on 2026-09-21 (A8): its FAULT[TEXT] lines are now handed to text-refine.txt as one scoped, picture-locked corrective round after the repair loop, so a prose fault the book audit reports is a fault the rewriter must be equipped to close — and, because the pictures are final by then, a fix the audit asks for may never be a move of text between pages.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: The Jev text audit (jevAudit.js, wired into textRefine.refineStoryText 2026-09-27) flags a page for each AI-slop type in proseSlop.SLOP_TYPES, and the page goes to the one repair pass. Each type carries its writer rule and its Jev question side by side; SLOP_RULES fills STYLE_RULEBOOK, which reaches the beats writer, the trial writer and the text repair through {STYLE_RULEBOOK}. A slop type Jev judges that the writer was never told is a finding no first draft can avoid; a rule the writer gets that Jev does not judge is unmeasured. Change a type in proseSlop.js, never in one template or in the Jev question file.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: avatar-evaluation.txt gates avatars generated from avatar-main-prompt.txt; a criterion the judge rejects on must be an instruction the generator carries, or the retry loop burns paid calls chasing a rule nobody stated.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: The 2x4 avatar sheet is generated by the row builders in character2x4Sheet.js (buildBodyRowPrompt, buildHeadRowPrompt, buildStyleTransferPrompt) and judged by four templates. Two hazards, both measured on staging job_1790100385959_1nitlympp: a pose the generator asks for that a judge does not know (cell 4/8 rear turn, filled from REAR_TURN_POSE into both sides since 2026-09-23), and a degenerate-judge fix that lands on one judge only (the 2026-08-12 echo guard reached the style judge and not the three row judges, which then copied their example on 6/6 sheets). isEchoedJudgeVerdict/askSheetJudge is the one guard all four use.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: empty-scene-qc.txt is validateEmptyScene's judge of the plate empty-scene.txt paints; a check the judge applies that the plate author was never given is a blind grade, which is exactly how the reserved-corner and geometry findings arose. The shared half stays shared: GEOMETRY_DIMENSIONS (sceneGeometry.js) writes the author's geometry block and the judge's {GEOMETRY_CHECK} from one source. Extracted from evalPipeline.js string literals on 2026-09-15. Since 2026-09-25 plate-derive.txt (the camera-move / re-light edit of a vantage's base plate, prompts.js buildPlateDerivePrompt) is a generator of the same judge, and the edge-to-edge / no signature / no mat rule is one source: shotVocabulary.PLATE_EDGE_RULE fills {PLATE_EDGE} in both generators, and its PLATE_MARKS / PLATE_SURROUNDS fill the judge's Wrong text and Frame edge checks. Since 2026-09-26 the landmark REFERENCE line is one constant too (shotVocabulary.PLATE_LANDMARK_REFERENCE fills the author's **REFERENCE:** line and the judge's LANDMARK_CHECK), and PLATE_PEOPLE fills both the author's PLATE_NO_PEOPLE_RULE and the judge's Figures check. Since 2026-09-26 the judge's STRUCTURE_CHECK (check key `structures`, soft) quotes the two rules the author's STRUCTURES block is built from (prompts.js PLATE_STRUCTURE_MATCH_RULE, PLATE_STRUCTURE_PART_RULE); that block is written in JS (buildPlateStructuresText), not in empty-scene.txt, so the generator half of this rule lives in server/services/prompts.js.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: A page's time of day and weather are its brief's `timeOfDay` / `weather` fields (server/lib/sceneLight.js, owner 2026-09-24). image-generation.txt carries them as the page's LIGHT line and empty-scene.txt as the plate's; image-semantic.txt (DECLARED LIGHT), empty-scene-qc.txt (LIGHT_CHECK) and the visual-flow judge in styleConsistency.js judge the render against the same two fields. A light rule a judge applies that the illustrator was never given — or a judge that goes back to reading the hour out of prose — is the blind grade this pair exists to prevent. The shared half is one module: every line on both sides is built from sceneLight.js. Since 2026-09-26 the weather owns the sky: lightParts composes time × weather, a covered weather's phrase names no sun, moon or blue sky (COVERED_SKY_CLAUSE), and the judges read describeLightForJudge — the labels plus that same sky phrase — so a sun in a fog page is judged against the words that forbade it.

sets.axis: first render vs every repair that repaints pixels
sets.reason: The page prompt carries the page's LIGHT line; a repair that repaints the frame and is not told the light repaints it at will — staging job_1790277448294_5herh01j7 p15 declared night + fog, the round-1 inpaint was sent only 'remove the street lamp' and came back in golden daylight (2026-09-25). Every repaint builder closes on sceneLight.buildRepairLightLine, read from the brief's fields: the page inpaint (images.js buildInpaintInstruction, also the manual /repair/image route), the character repair (faceRepair.js buildPrompt, every branch) and the scale repair (scaleRepair.js buildScaleRepairPrompt). Iterate and the regenerate fallback re-render from the full page prompt and carry the page's own LIGHT line. A new repaint path joins this set.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: cover-evaluation-notes.txt is the cover-only preamble the evaluator is given (viewer gaze, flat title, and the text regime), and cover-composition.txt plus the cover hint assembly in coverIterate.js is what the cover was painted from; a text or gaze rule tightened on one side and not the other scores a cover for a brief it never had. Extracted from evalPipeline.js string literals on 2026-09-15 so this pair can name a path instead of a 5,000-line module. Widened 2026-09-23: a cover is also judged by the semantic judge (image-semantic.txt, via evalPipeline.js's cover branch), consolidated by feedback-consolidator.txt (repairPipeline.js), and its structured {TEXT_RULES} comes from requiredText.js. None of the three carried the baked title, so on staging job_1790100385959_1nitlympp the semantic judge filed the correctly painted title as CRITICAL, the consolidator ordered it removed and the front cover shipped without one (docs/audits/prompt-audit-2026-09-23/09-covers.md C1). The title generator itself is buildCoverPrompt/bakedTitleLine in promptBuilders.js, not listed here because every commit touches that module. Since 2026-09-23 the title is a required-text item (requiredText.coverRequiredTexts) in every judge's {TEXT_RULES}, the consolidator input and the inpaint clause, and the generator's title block is headed REQUIRED TEXT — change the title contract there, on both sides at once. Since 2026-09-24 a FULL-STORY cover is a page (covers-as-pages): what it is painted from is the Art Director's brief of its cover beat, and the beat's cover facts (gaze at the viewer, the copy-space textPosition, the element budget) live in coverBeats.js — a generator of this set. cover-composition.txt and coverIterate.js now paint the TRIAL cover only.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: clothing-review.txt reviews the wardrobe contract story-bible-from-beats.txt writes (buildClothingReviewPrompt fills {CURRENT_CLOTHING} from the bible's used outfits) and rewrites it before the styled avatars start. A check the reviewer applies must be a rule the bible writer was given, and a bible rule the reviewer never checks is a rule nobody enforces: on 2026-09-23 the audit found the plot-worn-object rule and the base-layer variety under a removed outer layer with no reviewer check, and the reviewer dressing non-cast creatures because nothing told it only the listed characters have a wardrobe (docs/audits/prompt-audit-2026-09-23/03-wardrobe.md F3-F5); checks 9, 11 and 12 now carry them. Both templates also read the same wardrobe-scoped brief and cast (promptBuilders wardrobeStoryBrief / wardrobeCharacterDetails). Garment WORDING is owned by this contract (docs/decisions.md 2026-09-23): the Art Director's page briefs (scene-briefs-all.txt) select versions and copies words, and clothingCheck.js makes a linked Visual Bible entry adopt the contract's clause. Since 2026-09-26 both read GARMENT_ONE_OUTFIT_RULE (promptBuilders): a garment belongs to the outfit of the character who wears it first, and a plan handoff lives in the plan line and wornItems, never in a second outfit (staging job_1790373080139_vnx5l8iy7: the reviewer's check 12 copied one brother's jacket into the other's outfit).

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: arc-panel.txt walks the committed arc lens by lens and names what the creator missed; arc-create.txt writes the arc and arc-retell.txt rewrites it against the panel. A lens the panel scores by must be a fault-shape the creator and the re-teller were GIVEN — otherwise the arc is corrected after the fact instead of written right, which buys a fault the generator could have avoided at the price of a whole extra round trip. The creator's and re-teller's critique is ONE constant, arcCritiqueSpec() in promptBuilders.js, filled into both as {ARC_CRITIQUE_SPEC}; {TELLING_RULES} and {ARC_LOGIC_SPEC} are the same pattern. The panel's ENTRANCE, ASSUMED, SENSE and PLACE lenses read the SAME strings the creator gets (ARC_ENTRANCE_RULE, ARC_GIVEN_RULE, ARC_SENSE_RULE, ARC_PLACE_RULE). Since 2026-09-24 (logic-first arc, one arc) the panel's FIRST lens is LOGIC, which reads ARC_LOGIC_CHECK — the same constant that defines a fault in the creator's critique — against the STORY LOGIC block the creator writes before its sentences; since 2026-09-25 both write a finding the same way, quoting the conflicting words (ARC_FINDING_RULE, one constant in both), and code drops a panel finding whose quote is not in the arc (filterPanelFindings, beatsPipeline and the Lab mirrors); and since the same day (owner: "Ask each panel to output the three worst issues. Tagging a sentence is no good; an issue can be spread over many sentences.") both report their THREE worst issues in ONE line shape (ARC_ISSUE_RULE, arcIssueLine, ARC_ISSUE_MAX), each citing every sentence it concerns, parsed by ONE parser (parseArcIssues) for the panel and the critique; the CAST and ACTION lenses left the same day, because both were counts (the (new) figures are counted in code, each child's action by plan-check Q12). Since 2026-09-25 (arc prompts v3) the creator's principles (arcPrinciples) state ARC_EXCITING_DEF and ARC_MAIN_TURN_RULE, and the critique's second fault family ARC_PART_CHECK (a main character with no turn, an opposition that never acts) is the critic half of the same pair; every commissioned character's scene is the page plan's (stage split), so the panel has no ACTION lens. Since the same evening (variant B, Lab #1490) arcPrinciples states EVERY_CHILD_ACTS_RULE to the creator and the re-teller as a GENERATOR rule with no arc critic lens, deliberately: the variant measured in #1490 had none, a lens would send a MAJOR finding into the re-telling round the measurement did not include, and the rule's critic is plan-check Q12 (each commissioned character's ACTION line on the pages), whose finding the re-plan must fix. A new lens is written the same way: its rule is a constant the creator's TELLING_RULES, ARC_LOGIC_SPEC or STORY SHAPE also carries. arc-hints.txt is a critic too: it reads the settled arc and, since 2026-09-24, its STORY LOGIC ({STORY_LOGIC}), and a CHANGE that contradicts the logic must name the fact it changes, because the hint steers the planner. Since 2026-09-26 the panel's STAKES lens and the critique's third fault family read arcStakesRules(inputData) — ARC_OPPOSITION_HOLDS_RULE (off the simple bands) and ARC_QUESTIONS_ANSWERED_RULE — the SAME strings {TELLING_RULES} gives the creator and the re-teller (staging job_1790446348343_z3fw660ie: an opponent whose own limit emptied the turn, and a prize whose keeper the ending left open, with no critic of either rule); and ARC_SEVERITY_DEF makes an action at the turn or climax that could not happen at least MAJOR, the critic half of ARC_SENSE_RULE.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: plan-check.txt checks the page plan story-beats.txt produces; a constraint the checker counts must be a constraint the planner was told to satisfy.

sets.axis: Test Lab stage vs production call site
sets.reason: The page plan's re-plan round runs in production in beatsPipeline.js (buildReplanSection, replanKeepPages, reviewPlanChanges, the recheck and replanRoundRegressed) and is mirrored by the Lab's beats_replan stage in testlab.js (runBeatsReplanStage, analyzeReplanCompliance). A re-plan argument passed on one side only makes the Lab measure a round production never runs. Found 2026-09-25 while adding the commissioned span floor (castFloor) to both, on Lab #1494. Since 2026-09-27 the Lab no longer mirrors the round: it calls the run's own Step 2 (makePlanReader, planCheckInputs, createPlanCheckRunner, runReplanRounds), and tests/unit/lab-prod-call-parity.test.ts compares the two call sequences.

sets.axis: Test Lab stage vs production call site
sets.reason: The planner's CAST block (owner, 2026-09-25, Lab #1495/#1496) is read off the first division by castCoverage.parsePlanCastBlock and threaded into the plan check, the counters (CAST_PROMISE_BROKEN, with the check's ACTION lines and the focus character from pickMainCharacters) and the re-plan — in production by beatsPipeline.js and in the Lab's beats_replan stage by testlab.js runBeatsReplanStage. A table threaded on one side only makes the Lab measure a round production never runs.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: A page can declare one of a character's garments OFF. image-generation.txt states the removal to the illustrator and wardrobeVariants.js decides which reference sheet that page is drawn from; entity-consistency-check.txt is the grid judge that then reads the result. Before the wardrobe-state split (2026-09-19) the judge was never told a state existed, so it read the garment off the reference cell and reported it missing from every page that correctly did without it. A rule about what a removal means belongs on both sides: the generator half says take it off, the critic half says its absence is not a finding.

sets.axis: heartbeat writer vs watchdog reader
sets.reason: server/lib/jobHeartbeat.js writes story_jobs.updated_at and server/routes/jobs.js is the only reader that kills a job for a stale one (two detectors, poll-time and stale-sweep); a change to when or whether the worker heartbeats, or to the timeout that reads it, is meaningless unless both sides move together.

sets.axis: strict iterate vs free iterate
sets.reason: scene-iteration.txt (the default rewrite) and scene-iteration-free.txt (the looser rewrite chosen when the composition is failing) are filled by ONE call site with one placeholder map; a rule or placeholder added to one is silently absent on whichever template that page's iterate selected.

sets.axis: first Art Director vs rewrite Art Director
sets.reason: A page brief is authored at FOUR sites: the two Art Director templates that write it the first time, and the two iterate templates that REWRITE it when the render proves it unbuildable. The rewrite replaces the brief wholesale and becomes the page's contract with the image model, so a rule only the first author holds is a rule one repair round deletes. Measured 2026-09-17 over the 11 stored iterate rounds of staging job_1789584708605_rts4wqupm and job_1789506283204_3kxqshifx: 11 of 11 rewrites dropped `shot`, `landmarkView` and every character's `depth` and `looksAt`, and emitted no `wornItems` row at all, where the brief each replaced carried all of them. This set is why that cannot happen silently again: touch an Art Director template and the gate asks what the rewriter gets.

parity.anchorsNote: Placeholders, not prose: each is ONE exported constant filled at all four sites, so the anchor proves the rule reaches the template and tests/unit/ad-iterate-parity.test.ts proves the constant reaches the BUILT prompt byte-identically. Three iterate-only placeholders stay deliberately unanchored because they have no Art Director counterpart to keep in step: {OBJECT_ID_STABILITY} (the Art Director MINTS the ids, so it has none to substitute), {DECLARED_TRAIT_VERBATIM} (declared where the drift was measured — see DECLARED_TRAIT_VERBATIM_RULE), and {MAX_CHARACTERS_PER_SCENE} (the image model’s face cap, which the Art Director expresses as its own staging rules). {STAGED_PROP} left the anchors on 2026-09-23: it is a page-TEXT rule, and the all-pages Art Director runs before any page text exists (owner) — the three sites that see the text carry it, pinned by tests/unit/brief-authoring-contracts.test.ts.

sets.axis: Test Lab stage vs production call site
sets.reason: The arc re-telling runs only when a quoted MAJOR or CRITICAL issue survives (the create critique's three worst or a panelist's three worst), and is handed only those issues, duplicates across panelists merged (owner, 2026-09-25; Lab #1459-1467: every re-telling that answered MINOR findings was judged worse). Production (beatsPipeline.js, the arc machine's round loop) and the Lab mirrors (testlab.js arc_effort stage 'pipeline' and arc_panel_replay params.retell) all call the ONE gate, arcRepairFindings with splitCommittedBlock in promptBuilders.js, through jevAudit.arcRepairFindingsWithCastCheck since 2026-09-27 (the gate is decided by the critique and the panel alone; the Jev cast check only adds FEEDBACK lines to an already-open re-telling, owner 2026-09-27); the re-telling's creator call is beatsPipeline.makeArcCreatorCall, which the Lab arc_panel_replay imports (2026-09-27); a mirror that re-tells ungated measures a call production no longer makes.

sets.axis: authored-brief correction vs rewritten-brief correction
sets.reason: A brief's mechanical findings are answered on two paths — the one brief re-ask on the authored path (briefChecks.js; the scene review in beatsPipeline.js until 2026-09-28) and the corrective re-ask on the rewrite path (images.js iteratePageCore) — and the second was a hand-rolled copy of the first that measurably did not work: over the 11 stored iterate rounds of staging job_1789584708605_rts4wqupm and job_1789506283204_3kxqshifx it fired once per page and resolved findings on ZERO of them, because it sent the findings without the text being corrected, accepted on a COUNT (a correction that swaps one fault for another scores equal and is rejected), and re-asked the same model that had just failed the contract. Owner, 2026-09-17: 'All 3 same as pipeline. These should be siblings or even identical code.' The payload contract (assertCorrectorSeesText), the introduced-vs-survived verdict (judgeCorrection) and the model name (MODEL_DEFAULTS.briefCorrectionModel) are now ONE implementation in server/lib/briefCorrection.js; this set is what stops a call site drifting off it again.

sets.axis: generation-time identity lines vs iterate / char-repair / cover identity lines
sets.reason: Four builders assemble the expectedCharacters the SoM identity call names figures from — storyJobPipeline.js phase 5b-pre (generation), images.js iteratePageCore (iterate), charRepairTarget.js buildPageCast (character repair) and coverIterate.js buildExpectedCoverCharacters (covers). Each entry needs name, description, clothing AND position: the sanitized SoM tier strips the "Wearing:" tail out of the description and rebuilds the wardrobe from the clothing field, and the position field is the only cue left when a figure is drawn in another character’s clothes and hair. The generation builder was given both on 2026-08-22 and the other three were not, so every iterate, repair and cover detection ran on appearance alone — measured on job_1789681157795_wkt20ckod p12 v1, where that cost a two-child name swap and a page scored 0 on findings attributed to the wrong figure.

sets.axis: text reply guard vs image reply guard
sets.reason: textReplyGuard.js and imageReplyGuard.js are the same allow-list judgement over the same provider vocabulary on the two halves of the pipeline; imageReplyGuard IMPORTS NATURAL_STOP / TRUNCATING_STOP_REASONS / REFUSING_STOP_REASONS from textReplyGuard so there is one copy, and a reason class added or reclassified on one side without the other means a refusal is loud on text and silent on images (or the reverse) - the 2026-09-18 split, where the text path was inverted to an allow-list in a5052d176 and the image path's two-value refusal test was left standing in the same tree.

sets.axis: page worn-vs-held vs cover worn-vs-held
sets.reason: The page path (buildImagePrompt's REQUIRED OBJECTS loop, promptBuilders.js) and the cover path (applyCoverWornHeldDedupe, coverIterate.js) each answer the same question - is this element worn on a body, or held/placed off it - for the SAME Visual Bible entries of the SAME story. They drifted for seven weeks: the page side inferred the verdict from a prose verb regex while the cover side rode the structured cover-hint 'holds:' field and on 2026-09-15 (566042c10, 80548cfd5) deliberately left its token matcher loose and moved the verdict onto declared slot identity. The page side's regex was deleted on 2026-09-18 for 0.73% precision over 247 stories. A worn-vs-held rule added to one resolver and not the other puts the same garment on the body on the cover and in the hero's hands on page 5.

sets.axis: mechanical clothing findings: producer vs the prompt that fixes them vs the Lab mirror
sets.reason: clothingCheck.js decides WHICH clothing faults are sendable (REVIEWABLE) and words each one as its own fix; briefChecks.js sends them, with REASK_CLOTHING_EXTRA and clothing_incomplete, to the one brief re-ask. A type added, removed or re-worded in one is silently absent or stale in the other - on 2026-09-18 the deletion of outfit_misattributed left the scene review's check 0 instructing a garment move that could never be asked for. The scene review and its Lab replay (a hand-copied type list) were members until both were deleted on 2026-09-28.

sets.axis: the six templates that author or judge a page against its text
sets.reason: A page's text may name several characters and several actions; its picture stages one moment, the one its brief names. Settled twice (docs/SETTLED.md, 2026-09-13: semantic eval judges image-vs-BRIEF; 'the Art Director trims cast by design') and violated repeatedly, so the owner ruled on 2026-09-18 that the rule goes to every template that sees a page's text beside a picture - and as ONE constant, promptBuilders.TEXT_NOT_A_CHECKLIST_RULE, not eight hand-kept copies. Three partial copies already existed and had already drifted: image-semantic.txt's CHARACTER AUTHORITY paragraph covered characters and said nothing about actions, image-prompt-compliance.txt's STORY_TEXT DECLARES NOTHING block covered characters and dialogue and said nothing about actions, and book-audit.txt stated it only inside one weight's definition. The rule carries a SECOND half the first must not erase - a character the story gives a moment of their own that no page's plan line ever stages is a fault against the PLAN - because a first-half-only rule would excuse staging job_1789681157795_wkt20ckod, where an invented antagonist fell out of the plan across three pages and three of that book's six CRITICAL faults followed. prompts/image-evaluation.txt is deliberately NOT a member (owner, 2026-09-18): it is handed no page text on any path - all three sites that build it pass a brief as ORIGINAL_PROMPT, and storyText is a separate argument only the semantic and compliance judges receive - so the rule could never fire there, and an unreachable line still competes for attention in the heaviest-deducting prompt in the system. Add it back only together with a call site that actually passes the page text. The same rule took prompts/scene-expansion-all.txt and prompts/scene-review.txt OUT on 2026-09-23 (owner): the all-pages Art Director and the scene review run before any page text is written and are shown none, so 5f, 12j and the reviewer's copy referenced a text they never see (docs/audits/prompt-audit-2026-09-23/04-art-director.md A10).

parity.anchorsNote: The placeholder, not the prose: ONE exported constant (promptBuilders.TEXT_NOT_A_CHECKLIST_RULE) filled at six sites across four files - promptBuilders.js fills three of them through two builders (buildSceneDescriptionPrompt serves both scene-iteration templates), and evalPipeline.js, sceneValidator.js and bookAudit.js one each. The anchor proves the rule reaches the TEMPLATE; tests/unit/text-not-a-checklist-reach.test.ts proves the constant reaches the BUILT prompt, because fillTemplate deletes an undeclared placeholder silently - and pins image-evaluation.txt as carrying neither the placeholder nor the prose.

sets.axis: wizard matrix vs prompt builders
sets.reason: The two matrix cell values that are NOT relationships - the auto-filled default (says nothing, emits no line) and the deliberate 'they do not know each other' choice (a fact, and it does reach the writer) - have to be recognised identically by the wizard that writes them and by every prompt path that reads them. The labels are already ONE table, shared/relationship-sentinels.json, so the strings cannot drift; the PREDICATE is written once per runtime (TypeScript for the browser, CommonJS for Node) and that pair can. The disease: the server compared the ENGLISH literal 'Not Known to' while the wizard stored the LOCALIZED label, so for de/fr/it the guard never fired and every cell the user had not answered reached the arc author as 'Levin is Nicht bekannt mit Max' - ten of them in one de-ch story, English never affected. A third sentinel, a re-worded label, or a change to what counts as unanswered (empty, legacy value, trimming) must land on both predicates in the same commit.

parity.anchorsNote: The three keys of the shared table, which every member must read: the JSON declares them, and each predicate module resolves all three (legacyNotSet folds into the unanswered set - a pre-split save is not distinguishable from the default retroactively, so it emits nothing). A fourth sentinel added to the table and read by only one runtime is exactly the drift this set exists to catch. The predicates themselves are named identically on both sides - isNotSetRelationship and isStrangersRelationship - so a call site cannot silently get the question it did not mean; that the two agree on every label in every UI language is asserted in tests/unit/beats-brief-relationships.test.ts, which imports the client module and the server module into one test, because an anchor cannot check agreement.

sets.axis: the peril ceiling and its historical exception, at every stage that states or judges it
sets.reason: The ceiling (nothing that could lead to death) is ONE constant, PERIL_CEILING_RULE in promptBuilders.js, filled as {PERIL_CEILING} into the arc creator and re-teller (via TELLING_RULES), the arc reviewer, the beats text writer, the text repair and both story-idea templates. It carries the owner's historical exception (4804fe357: a historical event keeps the danger it really had, told at a child's level, never removed). The exception once reached only the two idea templates; the arc, told to stay under the ceiling, invented a blunt rubber-tipped bolt for a historical crossbow shot and it spread to the outline, text, costume and Visual Bible (staging job_1791145238223_50osg2osm, 2026-10-05). A new stage that states the ceiling takes the placeholder; it never hand-copies the sentence.

sets.axis: which document outranks the saved character profile
sets.reason: Five prompts state what a saved character profile is AUTHORITATIVE FOR, and they must not disagree. The arc creator, its re-telling and its reviewer answer to the COMMISSION; the beats planner divides a settled arc and answers to the ARC. All four fill {CHARACTER_SOURCE_RULE} from characterSourceRule() in promptBuilders.js, with the planner and the hint pass passing master:'arc'. This set exists because the rule drifted the day it was written (2026-09-19): the split landed on arc-create and arc-retell, while story-arc-review still called the profile the source of truth — so the arc creator was told the premise outranks a saved detail while its own CRITIC was told the opposite. The motivating story is staging job_1789759147125_p08djwhbl, whose premise stages four boys meeting as strangers over one egg while every profile calls them good friends. It drifted a second time the same way: arc-hints.txt, a FIFTH stage reading the same saved profiles beside the settled arc, was never given the rule at all, and on job_1789853503332_riqncqg1i it emitted a CHANGE undoing the first meeting the arc staged — the hint rides into buildBeatsPrompt, and the planner obeyed it over the arc. arc-panel.txt joined on 2026-09-23 as a SIXTH reader of the same saved profiles (it fills {CHARACTER_DETAILS} beside the committed arc) that carries NO {CHARACTER_SOURCE_RULE}: decisions.md 2026-09-19 left it out because it 'makes no source claim, so cannot contradict'. It is a member so a change to how profiles are framed is weighed there too; whether it should carry the rule is an owner question (docs/audits/prompt-audit-2026-09-23/01-arc.md B).

sets.axis: who applies an arc hint the other side could not
sets.reason: The SAME arcHints string is injected into two stages under two headings that form one contract: the beats planner applies what a picture can hold, and the text writer applies 'what the beats have not'. If one heading changes without the other, a hint is either dropped by both or honoured twice. Both headings are built in promptBuilders.js (buildBeatsPrompt's ARC_HINTS and the text builder's ARC_HINTS), not in the templates. The planner's half was a bare imperative until 2026-09-19: measured over the 42 CHANGE lines stored across 14 staging runs, 16 mandate a figure's continued presence against the three-named cast cap and 10 mandate simultaneity against 'two characters given different actions at one instant lose one of them', so the planner honoured hints by breaking its own picture rules. The two critics that judge the hinted text read the same hints (2026-09-23): story-text-audit.txt (arc-informed) and text-refine.txt, under one heading built by buildCriticArcHintsSection with the same HINT_VS_ARC_RULE. Shown only the unamended arc, the audit faulted a page for following a hint and the refine rebuilt the contradiction the hint had removed (staging job_1790100385959_1nitlympp p15). The blind audit is denied the arc by design and so gets no hints. The plan check (plan-check.txt) joined as a THIRD critic on 2026-09-23 under the same buildCriticArcHintsSection heading: its question 13 asks whether each hint landed where its own words place it — on job_1790100385959_1nitlympp a hint anchored after an event was planned onto a page before the event existed, and the checker, never shown the hints, could not see it.

sets.axis: who counts as invented: the arc's counting rule vs the plan counters
sets.reason: The arc decides who is invented, and planCounters.js re-counts the plan against it (ARC_INVENTED_UNDECLARED / ARC_INVENTED_OVER_ALLOWANCE) through castCoverage.commissionedCast. Since 2026-09-24 the arc's decision is the FACTS section of its STORY LOGIC: one dash line per named figure the plot runs on, tagged (commissioned) or (new), defined by COMMISSIONED_CAST_DEF and UNNAMED_FIGURE_EXEMPT in arcLogicSpec() (promptBuilders.js, filled into arc-create.txt and arc-retell.txt as {ARC_LOGIC_SPEC}). parseStoryLogic reads the tags; the (new) names are the declared invented list and the (commissioned) names outside the character list are commissionedCast's supplied figures. This replaced the "Premise figures:" / "Invented figures:" lists of the critique. On staging job_1790100385959_1nitlympp the two sides disagreed twice: a dog named in a character's saved details and an unnamed one-page mother were both 'not counted' by the arc and charged by the counters, and the re-plan cut the mother citing the false over-allowance. A change to who counts must land on both sides.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: story-beats.txt states each page rule as an imperative and plan-check.txt audits the same rule as a question — the generator/critic pair for page division. The FRAMING is deliberately different and is not shared; the DEFINITION inside each was written out twice by hand, and a definition that drifts between the rule and the audit is a generator that cannot satisfy the judge grading it. Four of them are now single constants in promptBuilders.js (DEED_AND_EFFECT_DEF, TWO_HEIGHTS_DEF, NAMING_DEF, ENDING_EVENT_DEF) filled into both templates. WANTED_PICTURE_DEF is the exception: it reaches plan-check.txt only, story-beats.txt hand-states the equivalent as a planning question, and the pair is pinned clause-by-clause by tests/unit/plan-shared-definitions.test.ts. This set stops a further pair being hand-copied instead. Since 2026-09-23 two more are code-built and filled into both: the act spans by arc sentence number (arcActSpans, planner question 6 / checker question 4) and each character's own-action rule (castCoverage.castActionRule, the planner's {CAST_COVERAGE} / checker question 12); the appearance floor reaches the planner and the counters only, never the checker, which read a stated range as a cap. Since 2026-09-24 the over-the-shoulder contact rule (shotVocabulary.OTS_NO_CONTACT_RULE) is filled into both as {OTS_NO_CONTACT} (checker question 14): the planner had it alone and an over-the-shoulder page on a contact beat passed the check (staging job_1790277448294_5herh01j7 p12). Since 2026-09-24 castActionRule also carries the commission's central figure when the arc's STORY LOGIC names one (centralFigureActionRule): the planner's {CAST_COVERAGE} and the checker's question 12 {CAST_ACTION} read the same sentence, and question 12 asks an ACTION line for it. Since 2026-09-26 the whole-cast page rule is one constant (WHOLE_CAST_DEF) filled into the planner's one-moment list and checker question 17. Since 2026-09-26 the arc's STORY LOGIC reaches both from one builder (buildStoryLogicSection, with STORY_LOGIC_FACT_RULE): the planner's first division and re-plan keep every page to its facts, and checker question 18 names a page that breaks one.

sets.axis: the central-figure rule the planner and checker read vs the counter that counts it
sets.reason: The arc used to certify "the central figure acts in every third" in its own critique. Since 2026-09-24 the arc only NAMES the figure (the STORY LOGIC "Central figure:" line, stored as arcReviewReport.centralFigure); castCoverage.centralFigureActionRule states the rule to the planner ({CAST_COVERAGE}, story-beats.txt) and to the checker (question 12, plan-check.txt), and planCounters.js counts it (CENTRAL_FIGURE_ABSENT_THIRD, must-fix, direction 'more'). The thirds, the names and the presence test must agree across all four: a counter that measures a stricter rule than the planner was told files must-fix findings the re-plan cannot satisfy.

sets.axis: the group-page budget the planner is told vs the counter that counts it
sets.reason: How many pages may hold more than three named characters (owner, 2026-09-27; docs/decisions.md): castCoverage.groupPageBudget is ONE number — one page in six, at least one, raised only when the coverage floor cannot be met on pages of three. story-beats.txt states it ({GROUP_PAGE_BUDGET}, groupPageRule, planner question 3) and planCounters.js counts it (GROUP_PAGES_OVER_BUDGET, direction 'fewer', must-fix since 2026-09-27) on the same `present` list every cast counter reads. A counter holding the book to a number the planner was not told, or a planner told a number nothing counts, is the drift this set exists to catch. tests/unit/planner-group-pages.test.ts.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: The typed page plan (Lab experiment, 2026-10-05; docs/decisions.md 'Typed page plan'): castCoverage.typedPlanTargets is ONE object — the planner is told it up front (typedTargetsRule, filled into story-beats.txt as {TYPED_TARGETS} by promptBuilders.plannerTypedFills), planCounters.countPlanTargets counts against it, and typedPlan.js's per-page Jev questions quote the same one-moment definitions the planner is given (DEED_AND_EFFECT_DEF, TWO_HEIGHTS_DEF, WHOLE_CAST_DEF) and the targeted re-plan section restates the failed target. A target counted but not told, or told but not counted, or a Jev question whose definition drifted from the planner's, is the generator/critic drift this set exists to catch. shotVocabulary.PLAN_TYPES is the one type table both the counters (figure counts) and the shot assignment (shots per type) read. tests/unit/typed-plan.test.ts pins the parity.

sets.axis: single-idea idea prompt vs two-idea idea prompt
sets.reason: generate-story-idea-single.txt (one call per world, the live full-wizard path) and generate-story-ideas.txt (both ideas in one call) carry the SAME back-cover premise contract and the same [REVIEW] checklist; a rule or self-check added to one reads as absent on whichever template the request routes to.

sets.axis: the write paths that persist a user payload into a JSONB column
sets.reason: story_jobs.input_data is written by the full create (routes/jobs.js), the trial create (routes/trial.js) and three admin reruns (routes/admin/jobs.js); users.trial_data is written from the same trial character payload; testlab_experiments.results/params record the Lab's own. Every one of them copies values that were offloaded elsewhere, so the inline FALLBACKS travel with them — measured 2026-09-21, four columns held 133 MB of base64 across the two databases, and each column had at least one writer with no sweep. A guard added to one create and not its siblings leaves the column dirty through the other door.

sets.axis: unattended daily offload vs attended admin offload
sets.reason: The daily housekeeping routine (server/lib/dbHousekeeping.js, every environment at 03:30 CH with its own R2 credentials) and scripts/admin/offload-jsonb-images.js are two entry points to the SAME offload. They deliberately share one implementation (offloadJsonbColumn) and one bucket-versus-database guard (verifyBucketMatchesDatabase), so a scope, safety or reporting change made in one must hold in the other: the routine ran on two columns while the script ran on eight for a whole release, which is exactly how staging ended up with 38 rows nobody could clean. The attended tool may legitimately differ on budget (none, an operator is watching) and backups (it writes them) — that is what the Siblings-Checked vouch is for.

sets.axis: authenticated story route vs public shared viewer
sets.reason: a story is opened on two routes — GET /api/stories/:id (server/routes/stories.js) and GET /api/shared/:shareToken (server/routes/sharing.js) — and the shared/trial path in this repo has repeatedly lagged the full path by weeks. Both record the view through server/lib/storyViews.js; a field or a source value added on one side and not the other reads as absent for half of all views.

sets.axis: pipeline completion mail vs deferred trial mail vs reminder sweep
sets.reason: three senders build the SAME two things by hand — the greeting name and the claim link. storyJobPipeline.js (unified completion mail), server/lib/trialEmail.js (deferred mail on claim) and server/lib/trialReminders.js (the day5/day25 sweep) each resolved a first name and each decided whether to mint a claim token. The reminder sweep already gated on claim STATE while the other two gated on trial ORIGIN, and the greeting expression was copied at all three plus email.js — which is how every mail greeted users by their email address and how a missing require("crypto") killed the claim link on one path only. Greeting resolution now lives once in email.resolveGreetingName(); a change to who may be greeted, or to when a claim token may be minted, belongs at every member.

sets.axis: trial cover vs streaming cover vs iterateCover vs regeneration cover route vs trial page plate
sets.reason: Every cover render gets its landmark photo, plate and VB grid from coverIterate.buildCoverReferences, and its `use` ('render' plated-or-fail, 'edit' no plate and no photo, 'composite' unchanged) is picked at each call site: the trial and streaming covers and the trial page plate path in storyJobPipeline.js, iterateCover in coverIterate.js, the scene-composite cover route in regeneration.js. The trial cover once hand-rolled its own references and sent the raw landmark photo with no plate (prod job_1790169018278_n57xpnufo: strangers from the photo painted beside the child); a reference or plate rule changed at one site belongs at all of them. Since 2026-09-24 these are the TRIAL cover's sites only: a full-story cover is a page and takes the page path's references (storyJobPipeline preparePageData / images.js iteratePageCore).

sets.axis: Grok reference packing vs Gemini parts
sets.reason: What fills the scene slot is decided twice: grok.js packReferences promotes landmarkPhotos[0] only when no plate is given, and images.js's Gemini branch attaches the primary landmark photo only when no plate is given (since 2026-09-24; before, it sent the raw photo beside the plate). A change to when a raw landmark photo may reach a render belongs on both providers.

sets.axis: plate photo packing (grok.js) vs plate prompt budget (images.js)
sets.reason: A landmark plate's photo is centre-cropped to the plate aspect with no magenta pad and no magenta prefix (owner, 2026-09-26, decisions.md; reverses 2026-06-16 for landmark plates). Two files hold the two halves: grok.js packReferences crops the plate source and refuses a plate call with padInputWithExtension on, and editWithGrok prepends the prefix only to a padded slot 0; images.js _dispatchImageGeneration turns the extension off for landmarkScene 'plate' (slot0IsScenePlate) and fits the plate prompt against the FULL cap because no prefix follows. Turn the extension back on for plates in one file and the other either throws or sends a prefix the plate fit never reserved room for (the 2026-09-25 over-cap bug). Every plate caller (vantage, per-page, trial, cover, iterate, Lab empty_scene) reaches this through generateImageOnly with emptyScenePlateRouting(); the derive/relight edit sends the base plate, not the photo, and is not part of this set.

sets.axis: page first render vs retry vs trial page vs iterate vs regenerate/test-models/style-lab vs calm-zone repair vs Lab mirror
sets.reason: Plate or fail (owner, 2026-09-24): a landmark page that is not cast-0 renders on its plate or fails, and only the declared roles in server/lib/landmarkScene.js ('plate', 'castless', 'composite') may take the raw photo with no plate. The rule is applied at every page render site - Phase 5a render and retry and the trial page (storyJobPipeline.js), iteratePageCore / ensureStoryPagePlate / the dispatch check (images.js), the calm-zone and regenerate repairs (repairPipeline.js), the page regenerate, test-models and style-lab routes (regeneration.js) and the Lab mirrors (testlab.js). A site that stops passing its plate or its role either fails every landmark page or, worse, is the one that quietly packs the photo again.

sets.axis: trial cover first render vs trial cover iterate
sets.reason: The trial keeps its own cover path (owner, 2026-09-24, covers-as-pages Q7 (a) / Q8): the trial cover builder in storyJobPipeline.js (startCoverGeneration, onCoverScene — front from the streamed cover JSON, back from the default hint) renders it first, and iterateCover in coverIterate.js iterates it afterwards. Both build the prompt with buildCoverPrompt and both refuse a full-story cover (coverIteratePath); a rule added to the trial cover's first render and not to its iterate — or the reverse — changes the trial cover the moment a user regenerates it.

sets.axis: full-story cover first render vs full-story cover iterate
sets.reason: A full-story cover is a page (2026-09-24): its first render (storyJobPipeline.js preparePageData / Phase 5a) and its iterate (images.js iteratePageCore, reached from the repair pipeline, the cover routes and the Lab via coverRender.iterateFullStoryCover) must apply the SAME cover-only options — coverRenderOptions (aspect, text always in the image, baked-title model, text contract, usage bucket) and withBakedTitle (the REQUIRED TEXT tail). An option honoured on one side only renders or judges the cover differently the first time and after every repair. Since 2026-09-27 the first render applies withBakedTitle through the shared page-render builder (server/lib/pageRenderCall.js makePageImagePrompt, also the Test Lab image stage) — pinned by the sibling set cover-page-render-baked-title.

sets.axis: full-story cover first render (shared page-render builder) vs full-story cover iterate
sets.reason: The REQUIRED TEXT tail of a baked-title cover (withBakedTitle) is appended by pageRenderCall.makePageImagePrompt on the first render (story run Phase 5a and the Test Lab image stage) and, since 2026-09-28, iteratePageCore (images.js) builds its prompt through that same closure instead of calling buildImagePrompt + withBakedTitle itself — the anchor is the shared call. A cover that gets the tail on one path only renders its title the first time and loses it after a repair, or the reverse.

sets.axis: generator-vs-critic
sets.reason: coverBeats.js writes a full-story cover's beat — the copy space as a textPosition (COVER_TEXT_POSITION) — and sceneBriefCheck.js checkCoverBrief holds the Art Director's brief to it (cover_text_zone_mismatch) before the scene review. Since 2026-10-05 the cover's gaze, shot, light, population and era are not the Art Director's at all: code writes them into the cover's FIXED block and pins them (jevBriefFields.coverFacts, jevDecisions.pinBrief), so cover_gaze_not_viewer was deleted and the beat no longer states the gaze. One constant feeds both; a cover fact added to the beat and not the check is unenforced, and a check the beat never states is a fault the Art Director was never asked to avoid. Since 2026-10-04 the place has two regimes: on the Jev path code decides each cover's vantage (jevBriefFields.decideCoverPlaces, beat says COVER_DECIDED_PLACE, the brief is pinned) and checkCoverLocations skips a `placeDecided` cover; on the backup the beat carries COVER_OWN_PLACE and cover_location_repeated holds the brief to it. Change the regime on both sides at once. Since 2026-10-04 a cover may also stand at an OFFERED landmark (jevBriefFields.materializeCoverPlaces writes it into the bible as a coverOnly wide vantage); the brief check reads it like any vantage.

sets.axis: every stage that reads the topic guide states its binding PROMISE the same way
sets.reason: Each adventure guide carries one PROMISE line (owner, 2026-09-25): what a reader of that theme must get — a dragon story has a grown dragon who is a character, present early and at the turn. It binds like the commission, so it is taken OUT of the guide body (which GUIDE_USE_RULE calls material) by stripGuidePromise and stated once by buildTopicPromiseSection, in promptBuilders.js. The readers of the guide are the arc creator and re-teller ({TOPIC_PROMISE} beside {STORY_BRIEF}, from buildStoryContextFields), the panel (its PROMISE lens) and the arc reviewer (story-arc-review.txt), and the idea call (server/routes/storyIdeas.js, beside the ADVENTURE SETTING GUIDE). Lab #1462/#1464 had no dragon character until the hatchling: the guide offered an egg as the centre, and nothing bound the theme. A stage that reads the guide without the promise section reads the promise as material again, or not at all.

sets.axis: Lab vs prod
sets.reason: The Test Lab image stage and the story run page render (storyJobPipeline.js Phase 5a) build the render call through the SAME builders in server/lib/pageRenderCall.js (owner 2026-09-27: the Lab must use 100% identical code to production). A change to how production selects grid cells, filters them, picks the model, builds the prompt, masks the copy space or sets the render options must land in pageRenderCall.js, where both read it; tests/unit/lab-prod-call-parity.test.ts compares the two calls.

sets.axis: Lab vs prod
sets.reason: The Test Lab eval stages (quality_eval, semantic_eval, eval_variance, the image stage's auto-eval) and the repair round's page eval build the batch input with the SAME function, repairPipeline.buildEvalInput, and the batch's per-page call with images.batchEvalQualityCall (owner 2026-09-27: the Lab must use 100% identical code to production). A change to what a page eval is handed lands there, where both read it; tests/unit/lab-prod-call-parity.test.ts compares the two.

sets.axis: Lab vs prod
sets.reason: The Test Lab empty_scene stage and the story run's plates (storyJobPipeline.js Phase 5a-pre-vantage and 5a-pre) run the SAME functions in server/lib/platePipeline.js (owner 2026-09-27: the Lab must use 100% identical code to production). A change to how a plate's prompt, mask, references, QC, retry or derive is built must land in platePipeline.js, where both call it; tests/unit/lab-prod-call-parity.test.ts compares the two calls.

sets.axis: Lab vs prod
sets.reason: The Test Lab char_repair stage and the repair round (repairPipeline.js executeCharFixAction) build the char-fix call with the SAME builder, server/lib/charFixCall.js buildCharFixCall (owner 2026-09-27). Inputs production derives (target box, guards, outfit, wardrobe-state sheet, axes, protection, clothing text) change there, never in one caller.

sets.axis: first render (story run) vs cover page vs iterate/repair vs Test Lab image stage
sets.reason: Every page and full-story cover image prompt is built by ONE closure, pageRenderCall.makePageImagePrompt (buildImagePrompt + the Grok VB-prose skip + a cover's baked-title tail). The story run (Phase 5a), the Test Lab image stage and, since 2026-09-28, iteratePageCore (every iterate/repair and the cover iterate) call it. The fixed blocks of that prompt are never cut, so a copy of the construction on one path drifts in size as well as wording: staging job_1790539784661_6mjcny1c7 lost its front cover and a p18 repair to prompt_fit_failed after the page compaction (docs/decisions.md 2026-09-28). A path that builds a page prompt another way joins this set or is deleted. Since 2026-10-05 the user-facing page regenerate and the Test Models / Style Lab routes (server/routes/regeneration.js) build theirs here too, with the grid from pageRenderCall.buildPageVbGrid (code review 2026-10-04 S1).

sets.axis: Lab vs prod
sets.reason: The Test Lab beats_scenes stage and the beats pipeline (Step 4b) run the SAME brief checks and the one Art Director re-ask, briefChecks.runBriefChecks, after the SAME two-call Art Director, beatsPipeline.runArtDirector (owner 2026-09-27: the Lab must use 100% identical code to production; 2026-09-28: the checks and the re-ask replace the scene review). A change to the checks, the re-ask or its verdict lands in briefChecks.js, where both call it; tests/unit/lab-prod-call-parity.test.ts compares the two calls.

sets.axis: trial page first render vs full-story page render: per-page clothing resolution
sets.reason: Both resolve each page's per-character outfit through buildSceneClothingRequirements (clothingResolve.js): name-tolerant and never defaulting to 'standard'. The trial page path hand-rolled an exact-key lookup with a silent 'standard' default, so a hero named LUNA whom the outline keyed Luna rendered every page of prod trial job_1790769860433_2bhhj0pyi in the standard avatar.

sets.axis: standard sheet vs costumed sheet (derive, generate, project, resolve)
sets.reason: A page that takes a garment off is drawn from an off-garment sheet: wardrobeVariants.js derives the off-set and its base category, styledAvatars.js redresses the base sheet, storyAvatars.js projects it into characterAvatars and resolveSheetForRef serves it, entityConsistency.getStyledAvatarForClothing serves it to the repair paths, and notEvaluated.js records a page that got none. Until 2026-10-04 every stage handled styled-standard/winter/summer and skipped costumed, so a garment taken off a costumed character was drawn from the costume sheet wearing it with no warning (staging job_1790446348343_z3fw660ie). A key-shape or category change on one stage must reach all of them.

sets.axis: wizard vs prompt builders
sets.reason: The wizard's live age line says which mains the server counts and whose age picks the band; client/src/utils/mainCharacters.ts mirrors pickMainCharacters (cap: 1 main for up to 2 characters, 2 for 3 or more; oldest main decides). A change to the cap or sort on one side makes the wizard promise a story the server does not write (2026-10-04: three books for a 2-year-old written for her 4-year-old brother).

sets.axis: every author of a page brief vs the provider-blocked rewrite
sets.reason: A costume's body (one tail and no feet, a covering top) is promptBuilders.COSTUME_BODY_RULE, filled as {COSTUME_BODY} into both Art Director templates, both iterate templates and the blocked-scene rewrite; an author without it rewrites a mermaid with bare feet (essbv p3 iterate, 2026-10-06).

withinFile.axis: streaming provider entry points (Anthropic / Gemini / xAI / OpenRouter)
withinFile.reason: every streaming entry point in textModels.js must throw streamCutError when its body ends without that provider's completion signal; the OpenRouter path accepted two cut page-brief streams as successes (staging job_1791145238223_50osg2osm, 7 of the last 40 staging beats stories). docs/decisions.md 2026-10-05.

withinFile.axis: streaming vs non-streaming provider entry points
withinFile.reason: every provider entry point in textModels.js must guard its prompt string; callOpenRouterAPI shipped without it while all seven siblings had it.
withinFile.excludeReason: callClaudeAPI is a dispatcher over the provider entry points, not one itself — it guards nothing because the callee does.

withinFile.axis: provider entry points (Gemini / Anthropic / xAI / OpenRouter, streaming and not)
withinFile.reason: every provider entry point in textModels.js must either deliver options.images (resolveImageInputs) or refuse them (refuseImageInputs). callGeminiTextAPI dropped them with a warning and the char-fix face gate judged blind for twelve days; xAI and the streaming paths dropped them silently (2026-09-27).
withinFile.excludeReason: callClaudeAPI dispatches to callTextModel, and callOpenRouterAPI delegates to callOpenRouterAPIStreaming with the same options — the callee resolves the images.

withinFile.reason: collectStagedFigures (names a Visual Bible figure onto the rewriter's locked cast) and partitionAnchoredObjects (lets a rewrite ADD a Visual Bible id) are the two sites that put a bible entity on a page; fa2cb3696 gated one on the bible's structured page range and not the other, so the creature the allow-list refused on p13/p16 was still staged there by its plan-line name. Both must consult vbEntityCoversPage.
withinFile.excludeReason: module.exports is the terminator that closes partitionAnchoredObjects' block so its body is measured exactly; it is not a staging site.

withinFile.axis: the page record vs the cover pseudo-page fed to the repair pipeline
withinFile.reason: storyJobPipeline builds the records the repair pipeline consumes at TWO sites: the per-page objects returned from the Phase-5a map, and the cover pseudo-pages pushed at `rawImages.push({...})`. They are read by ONE consumer (runUnifiedRepairPipeline, whose buildVersionEntry stamps v0 from whatever the record carries), so a provenance field the page side carries and the cover push does not is silently undefined on every cover. It has happened three times: `compressedScene` (added to the cover push after every cover root stored none), `modelId` (this set's anchor — the page path has carried `modelId: activeModelId` since it was written, the cover push carried nothing, so every cover's v0 recorded modelId undefined and no cover could say which model painted it), and the cover ROOT mirror further down the file, which moved `compressedScene` onto the shipped version and left `prompt` describing the first render. An absent field here raises no error anywhere, which is why all three survived. The block is measured exactly: `evaluationType: 'cover'` is the pushed object's last key and terminates it.
withinFile.excludeReason: evaluationType: 'cover' is the terminator that closes the push block so its body is measured exactly; it is not a record-building site.

withinFile.axis: the cover scene vs the stored cover record an iterate reads
withinFile.reason: A full-story cover's decided place (jevFixed, 2026-10-04, jevBriefFields.decideCoverPlaces) rides beatsPipeline's coverScenes into storyJobPipeline's coverImages record, which images.js iteratePageCore reads as the cover's savedScene to re-pin the location after a rewrite. A cover record built without jevFixed lets an iterate move the cover back onto any vantage, silently. The block is measured exactly: `briefedAsPage: true,` closes the record.
withinFile.excludeReason: briefedAsPage: true, is the terminator that closes the cover record so its body is measured exactly; it is not a record-building site.

withinFile.axis: the page record vs the iterate input the repair pipeline builds
withinFile.reason: iteratePageCore re-pins a rewrite from savedScene.jevFixed (pinBrief); the repair pipeline's own storyData.sceneImages whitelist lacked it, so no in-job iterate rewrite was pinned (essbv p3 v1: location, population and gaze moved, 2026-10-06).
withinFile.blockPattern: sceneImages: rawImages\.map\(r => \(\{|coverImages,  // a full-story cover's brief record
exclude: coverImages,  // a full-story cover's brief record
withinFile.excludeReason: that comment line is the terminator that closes the sceneImages whitelist so its body is measured exactly; it is not a record-building site.
